content.text:
Key points from the data:
- F3Z01's zone temperature rose by about 2°C from 2018-07 (average 25.1°C from July to December) and stayed there, whereas the other F3 zones showed the normal seasonal pattern (peaked in summer and then declined, down to 22.9°C by December).
- F3Z01's cooling setpoint remained constant at about 25.2°C. The pre-rising temperature was about 1.6°C below the setpoint. The post-rising temperature sits around the setpoint (only about 0.1°C below it).
- Damper opening setpoint: about 0.18–0.21 before July, then about 0.41–0.46 from 2018-07 onwards — sustained roughly double the cooling airflow demand — and it stayed there even through the winter months when the other zones' temperatures dropped. Temperature variability is sustained (not a flat drift).

This pattern — temperature pinned at the setpoint with persistently high damper demand — is exactly what an actual local load increase produces. A simple sensor drift/failure would not cause the controller to hold a persistently high damper setpoint in the winter. The data supports a local load change.
